name: Name
body:
A man walks into a bar.
"Stop me if you’ve heard this one before," he says. A pair of exquisite magelocks faintly glow beneath his worn leather duster. "You look like shit."
The bearded man hunkered at the table before him doesn’t look up from his tankard. "We’ve been here before."
The newcomer pulls up a chair, sweeping his long coat aside as he sits down and props his dust-caked boots on top of the table. "Creatures of habit, I reckon." Glancing over his shoulder, he gestures to the barmaid, twirling two gloved fingers in the air and then pointing at the table.
"I’d say it’s good to see you, Caine, but it never is." The bearded man empties his tankard without looking up. The heavy armor encasing his torso and shoulders creaks with his every move. "You got something to say, get to it. I’m on the clock."
"Everyone said you were dead, Mags."
The bearded man reaches up with his right hand, a mechanikal monstrosity attached to the stump of his severed bicep, and crushes the steel tankard in front of him. "It’s proving those bastards wrong that keeps me going."

name: Name
body: Asheth Magnus had seen it all. He had been a staunch patriot of Cygnar and the right-hand enforcer of his king, Vinter Raelthorne, before the coup that sent Vinter into exile. He had toiled as a mercenary to raise an army that would act as the vanguard for his king’s return, clearing the way for Vinter’s skorne invasion. And when wrongfully accused of treachery, Magnus had been tortured by Vinter’s paingivers before abandoning the exiled king. After this betrayal, Magnus, ever the advocate of Cygnar’s predominance, sought out the illegitimate child of Vinter Raelthorne in an effort to restore the rightful bloodline to the throne. And he was rewarded for his patriotism: pardoned for his crimes as a traitor and restored to a position of leadership in Cygnar’s military once more. After watching his protégé and greatest nemesis, Coleman Stryker, perish defending Cygnar from Khadoran conquest, Magnus made his penultimate stand for king and country against the Khadoran invaders, only to then make another as demonic creatures from beyond came for the very souls of all humanity. After that, he parted ways from the military machine he had both served and railed against for decades.

name: Name
body: The barmaid drops two fresh tankards on the table between the men, and Caine places a handful of coins in her palm with a nod. Eyes wide, she takes up the crushed mug. Caine quickly drops a couple of coins inside it and puts a finger to his lips, winking at her as she backs away. "So, you’re back to selling your sword—or whatever you call that," Caine says over the top of his mug, nodding toward the foot-wide legendary blade, Foecleaver, leaning against the wall behind Magnus. Beside it is propped a custom-built rocket launcher with a warhead already loaded. "Doesn’t look like you’ve given up trading bullets for pay days." Magnus pulls at his beard, his scarred blind eye catching one of the few rays of light penetrating the dank interior of the backwater tavern. "The difference is that I’ve been consistent. Only ever fought for one side." Caine raises his tankard in a mock salute. Magnus clenches his mechanikal fist, adjusting the tension on its actuators with his left hand. "Some’d say the same about me."

name: Name
body:
"They might, but they’d be wrong, wouldn’t they, Mags? You got into this business as an idealist—you had something to prove and a claim to stake. But you’ve served a lot of different masters, and each one of them demanded something different. So, you gave each one their pound of flesh. But now it’s hard to know what you stand for anymore. Then again, you were never in it for yourself." Caine shakes his head, perplexed, searching Magnus’ one good eye for some clue as to his motives.
"I did what I had to, when I had to do it." Magnus sets his empty tankard down on the table, perhaps a little too hard.
Caine shrugs, then nods, reaching forward and taking up the tankard before Magnus’ massive mechanika fist can crush yet another. "Not saying you’re the picture of redemption, but there’s a lot of people should thank you for some of things you’ve done. More than will never know."
Magnus raises both palms. "I never liked parades."
"You don’t like the benefits of wearing the livery, either?" Caine knocks back the rest of his tankard, pausing for an answer.

name: Name
body:
"That ain’t the world I fought for. Cygnar doesn’t have a place for me anymore." Magnus opens and closes his mechanikal fist. "I go where I’m wanted now. One for them, one for me."
"So, what now, then? If duty’s not calling your name, what are you getting out of this anymore?"
"Nothing but the coin."
Outside the tavern, an engine roars, growing closer. Panicked cries ring out; an alarm bell clangs.
Caine shifts in his chair, hands reflexively dropping to his sides as he looks over his shoulder for any sign of a threat.
"That’s my cue," Magnus says, pushing back from the table. Taking up the sword and rocket launcher behind him, his eye pulses briefly with arcane fire. "Time to go to work, Vic."
***
Among the shantytown that makes up Ternon Crag, the ramshackle tavern with its tilted shingle reading "Luck’s End" is arguably the most well-kept structure in the crumbling mining settlement called home by more transient ne’er-do-wells than upstanding residents.
With a rusty creak, the front door of the tavern opens. Magnus steps into the daylight, squinting as his eye adjusts to the brightness of the high-noon sun.

name: Name
body:
Before him is a belligerent pile of metal, posturing itself as an engine of war. A spiked cylinder filled with frenzied swine makes up its front, and a crude cannon mounted atop a sputtering, smoke-belching furnace provides additional power to the machine’s pig-propelled locomotion. Two farrow—repulsive, bipedal warthogs with more brawn than brains—control the meat thresher and its armament. Perched atop the contraption is a third farrow, hulking in mass compared to the others. He poses pompously with a massive cleaver held beside him as his crimson cloak flutters in the desert wind. With a guttural rasp, the tusked creature speaks, shamelessly butchering each syllable of its coarsely spoken Cygnaran with intermittent porcine snorts.
"Asheth Magnus," the farrow says, "Carver heard you were dead."
"A lot of that going around these days," Magnus replies flatly as his right leg shifts uncomfortably within the metal brace that supports it.
"Lord Carver is here to take this territory for Lord Carver’s empire." The farrow puffs his chest up proudly and gestures to his entourage assembled to the left and right of the meat thresher. Dozens of farrow brigands snort and squeal their support. A pair of massive creatures, abominable parodies of upright-walking wild boars with horrific mechanical limbs wielding enormous axes, screech with unrestrained bloodlust in their eyes. The farrow says, "You know of Lord Carver, B.M.M.D. Esquire the Third. Tremble before your conqueror’s might."

name: Name
body:
Unimpressed, Magnus scratches absently at his beard, taking in the mass of farrow troops lined up in front of him. "I gotta be honest. I know there’s a lot of your kind running around. But I don’t have time to keep track of all the shit-talking wannabes trying to make a name by thinking they can take a chunk out of something bigger than their worthless, piss-ant existence. So, no, I don’t know who the hell you are. And when we’re done here, I ain’t even gonna remember scraping your piggy ass off the bottom of my boot."
The farrow leader fumes, incensed, howling at the top of his lungs. "Lord Carver will not be disrespected!"
He slaps the cannon next to him twice, indicating the gunner should prepare to fire. "The Bringer of Most Massive Destruction will now bring most massive destruction upon you!"
"The only thing you’re gonna bring me is a pay day." Magnus hoists the rocket launcher onto his left shoulder, zeroing in on the platform beneath Carver’s feet.
The farrow gunner on the meat thresher fires early, its aim off. A burst of fire riddles the corner of the Luck’s End, shattering timbers. Without flinching, Magnus pulls the trigger on his launcher, rocketing the explosive projectile straight at Carver. The farrow leader squeals, dodges, and leaps to the ground as the rocket detonates on the cannon, shredding it to scrap.

name: Name
body:
Brandishing his oversized sword, Carver’s voice pitches higher, like a shrieking swine, the louder he yells. "Kill him!"
Spurred forward by Carver’s fury, the massive war hogs charge forward while the horde of farrow brigands open fire with their crude rifles. Bullets splinter the wood planking of the tavern, shatter glass windows, and ricochet off of Magnus’ power-field-protected armor.
Magnus wades into the fray, ducking and sidestepping a flurry of wild axe swings from the war hogs as the brigands swarm around him with hatchets and swords. He sweeps Foecleaver in wide arcs around him, slicing through the throng of bipedal hogs, who wail like injured piglets. But the pack of pissed-off pork is overwhelming, and Magnus takes a blow from behind by one of the war hogs’ cleavers. The power field generated by the arcane turbine on his back deflects what would have been a lethal strike to anyone else, but the impact still sends him staggering. He collapses to his knees.
Arcane glyphs encircle him and the ground beneath his feet goes soft, hindering his ability to move, as Lord Carver weaves a spell from the edge of the surrounding mob.

name: Name
body:
"Alright, Vic," Magnus mutters as he struggles to get his braced leg balanced underneath him. "I said it’s time to get moving."
Caine leans casually against the frame of the open tavern door, watching the skirmish unfold. He whistles, impressed, and nods toward a towering hulk of iron and steel as it lumbers out from behind the building. "Why, Magnus, I do believe you have outdone yourself this time."
With a chainsaw in place of its left arm, a wrecking ball chained to its right, and an enormous rocket mounted on its shoulder, the autonomous machine that approaches is the embodiment of war.
With a flash, Magnus summons a ring of glowing runes that dissolve into a wave of searing heat, cooking an advancing farrow alive. A second casting of the spell and a second farrow falls, but the mob keeps coming, and the war hogs, fueled by Carver’s sorcerous power, charge forward. The first war hog ducks low and gores at him with its massive tusks, sending Magnus sprawling face-down in front of a pair of frying pan-sized hooves.

name: Name
body:
"Invictus! Let’s! Go!" Magnus’ eye pulses, and fiery runes explode around him. Out of sight, a steam engine roars, and pistons seethe as the ground shakes with accelerating claps of metallic thunder.
Looming above him, the second war hog raises both cleavers over its head, ready to hack Magnus into thirds. A raging squeal bellows from its gaping maw just before its head disappears from its shoulders, momentarily displaced by a bladed iron sphere as big around as a cartwheel.    A fountain of hot blood gushes over Magnus as he rolls out of the way just as the headless corpse of the war beast collapses to the ground.
Using Foecleaver to steady himself, Magnus rises to his feet in front of a monumental assemblage of steam-powered hydraulics, gnashing gears, and armored plating. He glowers at it. "You got a loose cortex coupling or something?"
Twice the size of any standard military warjack, Invictus glares down at Magnus with baleful, burning eyes and huffs indignantly, steam billowing from the grill on his face.

name: Name
body:
Their consciousnesses linked through the unique bond only a warcaster and warjack can share, the senses of Invictus are as Magnus’ own. Through the enormous automaton’s eyes, Magnus clocks the remaining war hog charging from behind. Without turning around, Magnus focuses his arcane power into the warjack, charging the cortex that gives the machine life and empowering its weapons. Just before the war hog can reach Magnus, the chainsaw as tall as a man that makes up Invictus’ left arm spins up, its giant teeth blurring until they vanish. With only a small adjustment, Invictus repositions the blade directly in the path of the charging warbeast, and with a near deafening grinding of metal on metal, he shears off the right arm of the war hog.
The beast howls in rage and launches itself at Invictus with its remaining arm swinging its cleaver wildly. Magnus spins, eviscerating the warbeast with a backward slash from Foecleaver, then follows up with an uppercut from his mechanikal fist, connecting with the hog under its chin and laying it out cold.

name: Name
body:
Incensed, the remaining farrow brigands brandish their weapons and squeal furiously as they close in.
"You finish up. I need a breather," Magnus says to Invictus, stepping aside as the warjack stalks toward the onrush of rabid farrow.
His locomotive-sized steam plant bellowing, Invictus takes the mob head on. Twin plumes of fire burst from a pair of nozzles on either side of his face grill, and they set three of the brigands ablaze. Another shrieks in agony as it is crushed under a massive mechanikal foot, and with another step forward, Invictus swings his huge, bladed ball and chain in a wide arc, mowing farrow down like a scythe going through wheat. What few brigands manage to evade the warjack’s devastating attacks drop their weapons and backpedal in terror.
But wait, there’s more…
The engine of the meat thresher screams, fire and ash bellowing from its smokestacks as its spiked crusher cylinder begins to rotate under the power of the three dozen squealing boars within it. The crusher rips up the earth as it barrels toward Invictus, building speed. Stepping out from the sooty black cloud left in its wake, Carver appears, leveling his sword at Magnus.

name: Name
body:
"Prepare to meet the Hand of God!" Carver cries in swine-slathered Cygnaran.
Magnus sighs. "I forgot you were still here."
"When I sever your head and feast on your entrails, you will remember Lord Carver for the rest of your life!" Carver lowers his head and charges.
Magnus raises an eyebrow. "I think you lost something in translation." He raises his sword, ready to cross blades with the farrow.
Invictus turns toward the accelerating meat thresher, unleashing another gust of flame toward the massive battle engine. Undeterred, the thresher’s driver steams toward the warjack just as Invictus makes to raise his flail. But the vehicle’s pig-driven grinder is upon him too soon, mowing over the flail and sweeping under the crushing cylinder. Invictus lurches forward as his arm is pulled under the crusher, and the full momentum of the battle engine crashes into it. But the monstrous warjack plants his feet, digging into the earth, and upends the meat thresher, halting it entirely as the piggies within the cylinder tumble and squeal in distress.

name: Name
body:
Just steps before he’s in striking distance, Carver reaches behind his back and produces a short-barreled scattergun. He pulls the trigger, peppering Magnus with heavy shot that rips through his cloak and opens a gash in the flesh beneath his left eye.
Magnus swings Foecleaver before him, colliding with Carver’s Hand of God, stopping his charge.
"You got a cleaver, I got a cleaver," Magnus growls through gritted teeth as he backsteps and raises his fist. "You got a shotgun, I got a shotgun."
With a flex of his mechanikal fist, he fires both barrels of the twin-barreled scattergun mounted to his metal forearm, blasting shot into Carver’s face. Magnus spits. "Your kind has never had an original idea. You just pilfer from the labors of honest, hardworking folks, stealing their lives like the parasite that you are."
Flesh and tusks shredded, Carver launches forward with a series of wild slashes that bite into Magnus’ armor, opening wounds across his chest and legs. He staggers backward, unable to keep up with the farrow’s onslaught. The farrow leader is clearly elated. "Carver has an empire! Everyone will witness Carver’s greatness!"

name: Name
body:
"You got about three and a half seconds left before your little empire’s gonna be looking for a new emperor," Magnus says. Focusing his arcane power inward, he infuses his attacks with supernatural force, slashing Carver’s sword aside, then pummeling him with a series of blows from Magnus’ prosthetic fist, each time beating the farrow backward toward the meat thresher where it spins its wheels, unable to disengage from the entangling chains of Invictus’ flail.
"Let ’er rip, Vic!" Magnus shouts above the cacophony, even though he knows the warjack hears his thoughts clearly in his mechanikal mind.
Invictus revs his scrap saw and brings it down upon the chains binding the flail to his fist. A hail of sparks flies around the warjack as he severs the links. Freed from Invictus’ arm, the meat thresher’s crusher begins to spin. But the warjack stoops down, pushing his right shoulder into the crusher, letting the battle engine gnash its way over the warjack’s back before Invictus explodes upward to his full height, flipping the thresher onto its back.

name: Name
body:
Carver barely dodges the flaming wreck before it lands on top of him, but he uses Magnus’ moment of distraction to recover. Nearby, his eviscerated war hog stirs. Drawing on the life force still within it, Carver fills himself with arcane fury, magically mending his wounds and infusing himself with renewed power.
"Carver is all powerful." He glances over his shoulder at the warjack, twenty yards back, wary of being caught between the warcaster and his massive machine. But Invictus is mangled beyond any capacity to fight at the moment. His right arm is shredded, and his legs shudder as he struggles to stay standing.
"And you have nothing left, warcaster," Carver snorts before vaulting toward Magnus with his cleaver hoisted over his head in both hands. "Carver is victorious!"
But Magnus steps back, out of reach. "I’ve got one thing. Just was hoping not to waste it on you."
Carver yowls at Magnus’ retreat. "Coward! You flee from Lord Carver! The Bringer of Most Massive Destruction cannot be—"

name: Name
body:
Over his raging tempest of snorts and squeals, Lord Carver doesn’t hear the warhead launch from the shoulder of Invictus. In the space of a heartbeat, the Obliterator explodes at Carver’s feet, blasting a crater in the earth and engulfing the farrow in a blazing mushroom cloud.
"This little piggy shoulda stayed home," Magnus mutters as he limps toward Invictus.
The warjack hisses steam and clangs forlornly. Magnus pats the machine’s armored thigh, inspecting the damage. "Don’t worry. We’ll get you fixed up."
"Not bad for an old timer." Caine saunters toward them. He holds a fresh tankard in each hand and offers one to Magnus.
"Thanks. You never said why you were here," Magnus says, taking the mug.
"Same as you. To put that pig in the ground," Caine says, tipping his mug toward Magnus before taking a sip.
Magnus scowls. "Couldn’t lend a hand, then?"
"That’s the thing about wearing the livery. No bonuses for going out of my way. You know that." Caine admired the damage across nearly every inch of Invictus.

name: Name
body:
"I woulda cut you in." Magnus tips the tankard back, draining it.
"I don’t get it, Mags. There’s no amount of money that makes all this worth the pain," Caine says, scratching at his scalp. "You got no ideal to fight for, and you’re long past having anything to prove. What the hell, man. Give yourself a rest."
Magnus looks up at Invictus and wags his head toward the Luck’s End. "I can’t…" He trails off as he turns his back and slowly limps back toward the tavern.
"You can’t what?" Caine says, shaking his head, confused.
"I can’t…" Magnus pauses for a moment, letting Invictus catch up to him. "I just can’t stop."
